morphology.motility: Motile via anterior flagella and an undulating membrane, producing jerky/twitching movement

habitat.naturalHabitat: Human urogenital tract — vagina, urethra, prostate
habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human parasite; no cyst stage or environmental/animal reservoir
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Does not survive well outside the host; direct person-to-person transmission is required

microscopy.stain: Wet mount microscopy of vaginal or urethral discharge
microscopy.appearance: Pear-shaped, motile trophozoites with visible jerky motility and an undulating membrane on a warm wet mount

culture.media: Specialized culture media, such as Diamond's medium, in reference/research settings
culture.growthCharacteristics: Not routinely cultured in most clinical labs

identificationClues: Pear-shaped trophozoite with jerky, twitching motility on a warm wet mount
Undulating membrane along one side of the body
No cyst stage — trophozoite is the only form
Sexually transmitted; commonly identified on vaginal wet mount in symptomatic vaginitis

diseases: Trichomoniasis — vaginitis with malodorous discharge in women; often asymptomatic in men
virulenceFactors: Production of cytotoxic factors contributing to mucosal inflammation
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: One of the most common non-viral sexually transmitted infections worldwide; frequently coexists with other STIs and can facilitate HIV transmission
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Wet mount microscopy showing motile trophozoites is a rapid bedside test, though nucleic acid amplification testing is more sensitive

examFacts.keyBiochemicalReaction: Not a biochemical-test organism — diagnosed by wet mount or NAAT
examFacts.importantTest: Saline wet mount showing motile trophozoites; NAAT
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Jerky motility with an undulating membrane; no cyst stage exists for this species
